title: Building a Life Together — or On Your Own Terms

myths.myth: The right marriage will complete me.
myths.truth: A partner adds to a whole life — they don't fix it.
myths.explanation: Go in whole; a relationship can't be your missing piece.

myths.myth: Attraction is enough to build a life on.
myths.truth: Shared values and respect outlast the spark.
myths.explanation: Compatibility and respect are what sustain a partnership.

myths.myth: An arranged match means no choice.
myths.truth: You can bring values, questions and consent to any match.
myths.explanation: Love or arranged, the same compatibility lens applies.

myths.myth: Real love never has to be worked at.
myths.truth: Lasting partnerships are built with communication.
myths.explanation: Commitment is a daily practice, not a one-time vow.

myths.myth: Still unmarried? Something must be wrong.
myths.truth: A full life needs no marriage certificate.
myths.explanation: The 'still-unmarried' stigma is pressure, not truth.

myths.myth: A woman's clock means she must hurry.
myths.truth: Whether and when to partner is your call, not a deadline.
myths.explanation: The timeline pressure falls heaviest on women — and it's resistible.

myths.myth: Everyone should want children.
myths.truth: Choosing to be childfree is a complete, valid life.
myths.explanation: 'When are you having kids?' is a choice, not an obligation.

myths.myth: Her worth fades with her looks and age.
myths.truth: Worth isn't marital status, age or appearance.
myths.explanation: A person's value never expires.

myths.myth: He 'helps' with the housework.
myths.truth: It's shared work, not help — it's his home too.
myths.explanation: Naming chores as 'help' makes them her default.

myths.myth: Remembering everything is just a woman's knack.
myths.truth: The mental load is real work and should be shared.
myths.explanation: Planning and tracking the household is labour too.

myths.myth: His career naturally comes first.
myths.truth: Both careers count equally.
myths.explanation: Whose job 'comes first' shouldn't be decided by gender.

myths.myth: We sorted chores once, so we're done.
myths.truth: Fairness at home is an ongoing conversation.
myths.explanation: An equal home is renegotiated as life changes.

myths.myth: Marriage means you're always available.
myths.truth: Consent is ongoing — even with a spouse.
myths.explanation: 'Married = always available' is never true.

myths.myth: It's only abuse if they hit you.
myths.truth: Emotional, financial and sexual abuse are abuse too.
myths.explanation: Coercive control harms even without a single bruise.

myths.myth: What happens at home should stay private.
myths.truth: Abuse is never the victim's fault, and help exists.
myths.explanation: Silence protects harm; support lines and the law can help.

myths.myth: Walking on eggshells is just married life.
myths.truth: Fear and control aren't a normal part of a partnership.
myths.explanation: Constant fear is a sign to seek help, not to adjust.

myths.myth: Family should always come before the marriage.
myths.truth: A strong couple protects its own bond too.
myths.explanation: Honouring family and guarding your partnership can coexist.

myths.myth: Setting a boundary with elders is disrespect.
myths.truth: Kind, clear boundaries can sit alongside respect.
myths.explanation: Boundaries protect relationships rather than break them.

myths.myth: A new bride should just adjust to everything.
myths.truth: Adjusting goes both ways in a family.
myths.explanation: Joining a family is a two-way welcome, not one-way submission.

myths.myth: Couples should face family pressure separately.
myths.truth: Facing the family as a team keeps you both safe.
myths.explanation: A united couple-team handles the wider family best.

myths.myth: One partner should control all the money.
myths.truth: Money decisions work best shared and transparent.
myths.explanation: Joint planning beats one person holding the purse strings.

myths.myth: She doesn't need her own account.
myths.truth: Everyone deserves their own financial independence.
myths.explanation: Personal financial footing matters inside a partnership.

myths.myth: Big money calls are a man's department.
myths.truth: Both partners plan the big costs and goals.
myths.explanation: Financial decisions shouldn't follow gendered defaults.

myths.myth: Keeping you from money is just being careful.
myths.truth: Cutting off money access is financial abuse.
myths.explanation: Controlling all the money is a recognised form of abuse.

myths.myth: Having kids is just the next step you take.
myths.truth: Whether, when and how many is a real choice — make it together.
myths.explanation: Reproductive planning is a deliberate, shared decision.

myths.myth: There's always time to have children later.
myths.truth: Fertility has a timeline worth understanding.
myths.explanation: Fertility awareness and preconception health inform the choice.

myths.myth: Infertility is a failure or someone's fault.
myths.truth: Infertility is common, and there are real options.
myths.explanation: It's a medical reality, not a personal failing.

myths.myth: The family should get a son.
myths.truth: Choosing a baby's sex is illegal — and every child is equal.
myths.explanation: Son-preference and sex-selection are banned under the PCPNDT Act.

myths.myth: A real family is only the biological kind.
myths.truth: Adoption, fostering and ART build real families too.
myths.explanation: Family is made of care, by many routes.

myths.myth: Adoption is a last resort.
myths.truth: It's a first-class way to build a family.
myths.explanation: Adoption and fostering are full, valid paths to parenthood.

myths.myth: Only married couples can be good parents.
myths.truth: Single and LGBTQ+ parents raise thriving kids.
myths.explanation: Loving, capable parenting isn't limited by family shape.

myths.myth: The path to family is the same for everyone.
myths.truth: Gendered and legal barriers are real — and worth naming.
myths.explanation: Single men and others face extra legal hurdles (e.g. CARA rules).

capstone.name: Building Together
capstone.landing: A life built together — or on your own terms: the partnership, equal-home, family-map and reproductive-choice tools earned across Chapter 7, erased pressures shown as faint ghosts under the truths, Sam waving onward to parenthood.

canvasFeel: Adult / dark theme on the dotted-paper texture — building-a-life motifs (rings, blueprints, a forking path, a family map) glowing against deep violet night paper; struck-through 'settle down' pressures rubbed out by UN, equal-partnership truths written by RE.
